INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on July 20, 2022, via Zoom.
Commissioner Metcalf called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District One
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District Three
  Commissioner Vicki Perryman-Banks, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
Absent
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District Two
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant

Public Comments

 None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made the motion to approve the minutes from May 18, 2022.
Commissioner Banks seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Banks, Lesure, Battle, and Metcalf
  Nays: None

Special Presentation

  Jason Witt, Director of Community Engagement from Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium
provided his quarterly update report on the Hollywood Park Public Art Project. He briefly
discussed six (6) individual artists, their background, and informed the Commission that the
artists have completed their murals located in the retail section at Hollywood Park. Mr. Witt
invited Director Barnes and the Commissioners to an in-person viewing of the murals.
  Per Mr. Witt, the Alison Saar Project (a summer sculpture) continues to move forward,
sharing photos of progression with a scheduled date of full installation by August 9, 2022. Some
of the summer’s public performances included the Summer Bash 2022 honoring Juneteenth
making it the second year with performances by various artists from African drumming,
storytelling, interpreting, and tap dance.
  Mr. Witt also provided an update on Maren Hassinger’s project stating an internal
meeting was held to identify new locations for the pieces. He stated there is a lot more to come
from the Public Art expenditure that will be seen in the future.
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  Commissioner Lesure stated great report and update. He asked if the Kinsey exhibit is
still open. Mr. Witt replied yes and spoke of a newly installed contemporary exhibition to
compliment the traditional Kinsey Collection. He indicated he is working with Residency Art
Gallery to help bring in Inglewood and Los Angeles-based artists.

  Commissioner Battle stated she is glad to hear about progress towards a resolution with
Ms. Hassinger. She voiced her concern about the introduction to the Summer Bash stating she
hopes the Summer Bash won’t eliminate the honoring of Juneteenth. Mr. Witt stated he thinks
the Summer Bash would be better served on a different day.

  Commissioner Banks thanked Mr. Witt for another great presentation.

  Both Commissioner Metcalf and Director Barnes also thanked him. Director Barnes
asked the status of the bridge element that was expected in 2022. Mr. Witt's response was it will
trend towards 2023. Director Barnes asked if Ms. Hassinger was aware of the new location and
has any contact been made. Mr. Witt stated not yet. Ms. Barnes asked Mr. Witt to inform the
Commission on how the public is learning about the summer events. Mr. Witt stated Summer
Bash was publicized through the Inglewood newsletters, signage around the Stadium, press
releases, media alerts, and KJLH. Director Barnes asked for more clarity in the commitment to
consult with the Arts Commission. Helen Lessick requested a preferred day of the week for the
mural tour from the Commissioners. All agreed to a Tuesday at 10:00 a.m. Director Barnes
informed Mr. Witt she’d send him some dates. Ms. Lessick asked about artist fees, she stated
three temporary projects were held in the last three months of 2021 for about $177,000. Each
raises the question of the cost of the now smaller projects. She requested a more detailed
funding report be made.

Staff Reports

  Director Barnes presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission receive and
file the sponsorship request from Inglewood Open Studios, a private nonprofit artists'
organization, to support Inglewood Open Studios Tour 2022 in an amount of up to $9,950 to
fund banner production, installation and removal, weekend transit services and a photographer
to document the two-day cultural event taking place on November 12 and 13, 2022.

  Director Barnes gave an overview of the City's history of sponsoring Inglewood Open
Studios (IOS) and noted that sponsorship would still be recommended but not require the use of
Public Art funds. The matter is a City Council item and will go before them sometime in August.
Helen Lessick added the importance of this receive and file report stating this is a cultural event,
a private artist studio invite.

  Commissioner Lesure asked where are the banners going to be installed and for how
long. Director Barnes shared that the banners will be placed at various busy intersections and
  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

recommended the use of the WOW board. Commissioner Lesure asked how long the banners
will be up. Ms. Lessick stated in previous years the banners were installed a week before the
event and taken down right after.

  Commissioner Battle stated a week's notice is not enough time to inform or notify the
public. She reiterated the importance of the event stating it is an Inglewood event that has been
going on for quite some time and hopes that the banners can be picked up a week before the
event. Ms. Lessick commented different generational communities look at advertising differently,
the banners are great but there are various ways to advertise.

  Commissioner Banks stated in District 4 she only saw two banners and that may be due
to location. To be fair the banners should be spread out throughout the city. Commissioner
Metcalf added she is in full support of the organization and all they do.

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to receive and file the sponsorship request from
Inglewood Open Studios. Commissioner Battle seconded and the motion was approved as
follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Banks, Lesure, Battle, Lesure, and Metcalf
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Helen Lessick gave a verbal report on the following:
  - IGAP 2022: Art of the Trees update: an RFP Art of the Trees was issued on June
  1, 2022, a $30,000 Commission project for Public Art inspired by Inglewood trees.
  At this time there isn't a proposed site location yet. We have received 29
  applications, the deadline for entries was July 7, 2022. The artwork consists of
  public art, sculpture, installation, mixed media, and texts. The next steps include a
  three-member panel review, scoring applications, and identifying the semi-finalist
  artists who will be paid $300 to develop a notional proposal to include what they
  would do, where the artist would prefer to do it, and the type of budget. The
  process is currently in motion, one finalist and one alternate will be identified in
  late August or early September. The artist will then be contacted and have a year
  to complete this project. Director Barnes who was one of the jurors stated she was
  happy with the outreach that was made because we received a great response
  and was pleased to receive the 29 entries.

  Commissioner Lesure asked about insurance. Ms. Lessick responded this is a
commission contract requiring liability insurance, endorsing the city and its employees that is for
any project. The insurance cost is generally about $1,000 depending on the individual.
Commissioner Lesure asked if the artist are aware of the requirements before signing the

  3
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

contract. Ms. Lessick stated yes, artists have to sign that they have read, understand, and are
agreeing to the city’s standard terms and conditions and requirements.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner Metcalf read a list of upcoming city events with the Commissioners.
Director Barnes clarified the date of the Hispanic Heritage Festival stating it will be on
September 17, 2022, not the 18th, and stated Commissioner Lesure will be performing at the
Inglewood Jazz Festival on August 6, 2022. Commissioner Lesure looks forward to seeing
everyone on August 6 and 7, 2022 spreading love and light through the median of sound.
Commissioner Battle stated she will be there.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:21 p.m.
